strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Do not delay an available systematic source to fill a FEC block. Do not replace the live qualified RS path from iid-only simulator evidence. continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: Changed the product boundary from off|fixed|qualified-auto to current off|fixed with Auto deferred to future advanced research. Updated PROJECT_CONSTITUTION.md, ROADMAP.md, ADR-0005, PR #3 title/body and architecture contract tests accordingly. Third-party public services such as speed-test sites are now explicitly measurement baselines only; TLS Persona remains browser-like ClientHello shaping to an operator-authorized endpoint identity with normal certificate validation. Implemented internal/fec/simulator.go plus simulator_test.go and replaced cmd/wbd-fec-sweep with a deterministic fixed-schedule timing/capacity simulator supporting off, tail-block RS, micro-block RS and causal/sliding repair models, iid or two-state burst loss, fixed seeds, source-priority serialization, repair backlog, first-complete latency, delivery, wire ratio and drain metrics. GitHub Actions ci run 32851722051 completed SUCCESS with Go tests and handoff tests. Offline exact-code smoke at 20 Mbit/s payload over 200 Mbit/s / 50 ms RTT shows iid 10% causal 20:10 delivery 1.000 and p99 about 26.7 ms versus tail 20:10 delivery 1.000 and p99 about 33.4 ms; burst-length-4 at 20% shows causal delivery about 0.946 versus tail about 0.918 but causal p99 about 39.8 ms versus tail about 33.9 ms, proving iid wins cannot directly select the live codec. Capacity smoke shows 20:10 nominal utilization above 1 causes large repair backlog and recovery tails: at 140/200 Mbit/s payload/capacity, p99 rises to about 57 ms with roughly 270+ ready repairs; at 160/200 it rises to roughly 92 ms with 600+ ready repairs. Results and interpretation are recorded in docs/benchmarks/v2-fixed-fec-simulator-smoke.md.
continuation_cursor.current_task: Implement negotiated runtime FEC configuration epochs for the current product modes off|fixed without reconnecting DTLS/FakeTCP. Keep the live data codec on the already-qualified systematic RS path while the control semantics are added; do not implement or accept Auto.
continuation_cursor.why_now: The fixed-schedule simulator is repository-tested and has already exposed two important boundaries: causal repair improves iid tails at the same modeled ratio but does not dominate burst traces, and any fixed ratio that pushes total offered utilization above capacity accumulates repair backlog. The next product requirement is therefore explicit client-selected fixed/off policy with server ceilings and unambiguous epoch switching, not an estimator/controller.
continuation_cursor.done_when: Control frames can propose an explicit monotonic FEC config epoch containing off or a fixed profile; Auto/unknown values are rejected. The server validates supported scheduler/profile values and resource ceilings, acknowledges the effective fixed config, and keeps it pending until an explicit coding-window-boundary activation rather than switching mid-block. Duplicate/stale epochs, pre-auth proposals and overlapping pending epochs fail deterministically. Unit tests cover wire round trip, off/fixed validation, server cap reject/clamp policy as chosen by the implementation, monotonic epochs, pending-to-active transition and unchanged M3A-E behavior. Live transport integration remains a later atomic action after control tests pass.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: Extend internal/control with a new explicit FEC epoch config frame rather than overloading the legacy one-byte M3E ProtectionMode. Encode epoch + off/fixed + K:R + scheduler + flush/boundary-compatible fields; keep the reserved Auto value rejected. Add a server session wrapper with current/pending config and a boundary activation method, plus deterministic tests for auth ordering, monotonic epochs, duplicate/stale rejection, server resource caps and off<->fixed transitions. Do not change internal/fec live encoding behavior in the same commit.

product_policy.fec: client/session chooses off or an admitted fixed profile; server advertises supported code/scheduler versions and hard resource/wire caps; config changes use coding-window epochs. Auto is reserved future advanced research and rejected now.
product_policy.accounts: same username/account may own multiple simultaneous device sessions; live state keyed by account plus unique session id; prefer per-device high-entropy credentials and independent revocation
product_policy.routing: client capture modes off|global|only-cn|only-non-cn; mandatory underlay endpoint escape; Linux/OpenWrt use policy routing/prefix sets; Windows uses Wintun-class L3 plus broad routes or compact WFP/equivalent split classifier, never thousands of persistent firewall rules
product_policy.persona: ClientHello browser profile is client-selected from the server-supported set; Persona is separate real TLS 1.3 preflight. Endpoint hostname/certificate/private key must be identities the operator is authorized to use; public third-party sites may be measurement baselines but are not borrowed WBD identities.
product_policy.dual_lane: deferred until a one-lane fixed-protection cliff is measured; prefer striped/hedged independent repair with lane-specific equations/seeds/timing rather than byte-identical duplication; any >2x survival mode requires separate admission
